title: Conduction, convection, radiation
target: Identify mechanisms of heat transfer and support each classification.
criteria: Describe contact transfer, bulk fluid motion and electromagnetic transfer.
Recognize that more than one mechanism can act.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A metal handle warms because energy passes through the solid from a hot pan. Which mechanism is most directly described?
options: Convection of the solid handle as a flowing fluid.
Conduction.
A loss of energy conservation.
Only radiation through empty space.
cpa.guide: Conduction transfers energy through matter without bulk transport of the whole material.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A warm air plume rises above a heater and circulates through a room. What mechanism is this?
options: Convection.
Radiation only.
Mechanical energy creation.
Conduction only, with no fluid motion.
cpa.guide: Convection involves bulk fluid motion carrying energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A sealed vacuum gap reduces contact and fluid transfer between two surfaces. Which mechanism can still carry energy across it?
options: Conduction through absent gas.
Air convection through a perfect vacuum.
Only sound waves in the vacuum.
Radiation.
cpa.guide: Electromagnetic radiation can propagate without matter.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which observation specifically supports convection in heated water?
options: Colored tracer rises with warm water and sinks elsewhere in a circulating loop.
A thermometer alone reads a temperature.
A shiny lid reflects light.
The pot’s metal handle warms without moving.
cpa.guide: The tracer demonstrates bulk fluid transport; warming alone does not identify convection.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A person near a campfire feels radiation and warm rising air. Which statement is correct?
options: Convection cannot occur in air.
Only one mechanism is ever allowed in a real setting.
More than one heat-transfer mechanism can operate at once.
Radiation requires touching the fire.
cpa.guide: Real energy transfer often combines mechanisms.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A hot mug loses energy through its ceramic wall and then to moving room air; it also emits infrared radiation. Which account is best?
options: Only radiation exists because the mug is warm.
Conduction, convection, and radiation can all contribute.
Only conduction exists because the mug is solid.
Only convection exists because the room has air.
cpa.guide: Different parts of the transfer path involve different mechanisms simultaneously.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
